label: Atmospheric Entry
description: What entering an atmosphere does to a hull and the air around it — the physics layer that makes an arrival believable.

items.name: plasma-sheath
items.text: a full plasma sheath wrapping the hull, magenta-white ionization streaming aft into an incandescent wake kilometers long

items.name: shock-collar
items.text: a conical condensation collar flashing in and out of existence around the bow shock, vapor rings peeling off and dissolving behind

items.name: ablative-shed
items.text: ablative panels shedding in glowing flakes, a drizzle of orange-hot confetti raining off the heat-shield line

items.name: contrail-lattice
items.text: dozens of parallel entry contrails scored across the sky, each a straight white incision ending in a bright descending point

items.name: punched-clouds
items.text: a clean circular hole punched through the cloud deck where the hull came down, cloud walls still curling into the vacuum of its wake

items.name: boom-front
items.text: the visible pressure front of a sonic boom expanding as a ring below the hull, flattening grass, dust and open water as it passes

items.name: drive-distortion
items.text: the air beneath the hull wobbling with drive distortion, straight lines bending as if seen over a furnace, loose dust rising against gravity in slow columns

items.name: braking-burn
items.text: bow thrusters firing in staged sequence, hard blue-white braking jets stabbing forward, each pulse lighting the underside of the hull like a flashbulb

items.name: cooling-hull
items.text: leading edges still glowing dull cherry from entry heat, color draining from orange to iron grey as the hull cools, shimmer streaming off every fin

items.name: debris-halo
items.text: a halo of shed debris falling with the ship in loose formation, panels and ice glittering as they tumble in the shared slipstream
